items.title: IMF cites AI slowdown, spiking yields as looming global market risks
items.author: Pete Schroeder, Selena Li
items.creator: Pete Schroeder, Selena Li
items.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing risks from an artificial intelligence-driven selloff, rising government bond yields, or cyberattacks as potential threats facing still-resilient markets.
items.body:
The International Monetary Fund warned on Tuesday against "complacency" in global financial markets, citing risks from an artificial intelligence-driven selloff, rising government bond yields, or cyberattacks as potential threats facing still-resilient markets.
The IMF said in its Global Financial Stability Report that AI investments have so far [USN:L6N45R12W TEXT:"helped offset"] economic drags from war in the Middle East and overall policy uncertainty. But it noted "growing evidence" that AI capabilities may not require as much investment, or the potential economic gains may not be as large as expected.
"An AI market correction will affect the real economy," Athanasios Vamvakidis, deputy director in the IMF's Monetary and Capital Markets Department, said at a press briefing in Bangkok.
He said while global risk sentiment was very strong, underpinned by solid earnings and optimism about AI, such "resilience is not necessarily safety". An AI correction would have impacts on wealth and investment that could spill into broader markets, he said.
The risk of such a selloff, as well as a spike in sovereign bond yields or a major cyberattack, were among "plausible near-term catalysts" that policymakers should monitor, the IMF said in its report.
While each of these risks might be manageable on its own, they also could trigger vulnerabilities with potential systemic implications, Vamvakidis said.
Should the momentum in AI investment slow, the IMF noted growing leverage in the sector could exacerbate any shock by triggering forced selling and higher volatility. For example, hyperscalers now represent 10% of global investment-grade bond issuance, up from less than 1% in 2024.
"The consequences of an AI correction could be global," the IMF warned, as it called on policymakers to curb leverage use, including derivatives and margin loans, where it is "excessive."
RISING YIELDS The IMF said bond market risks have worsened since [USN:L6N40W0X6 TEXT:"its April report"], as higher energy prices have driven [USN:L1N45U12M TEXT:"government bond yields up"]. Historically high sovereign debt levels and unresolved fiscal deficits in major economies were adding to the pressure.
"The market is concerned about absorption potential of the huge issuance that is coming from the sovereigns and increasingly also from the private sector, at the time that central banks are shrinking their balances, and we have to rely more on price-sensitive investors," Vamvakidis said.
The IMF report said bond markets have so far dealt with the stress well, with hedge funds able to unwind some of their repurchase agreement borrowing without triggering turmoil in repo markets. The group called on policymakers to put public debt on a sustainable path.
On cyber threats, the IMF said that a lack of resources, particularly in emerging markets, and a growing reliance on a small number of critical providers was making [USN:L6N43I17J TEXT:"cyber defense more difficult"].
In over 70% of cases so far in 2026, software providers have had almost no time to patch vulnerabilities before they were exploited, a 20 percentage point jump from a year ago, the IMF said. It noted that while AI can help address some of these risks, models were also making cyberattacks more sophisticated.
The IMF cautioned that a major attack affecting a critical service or financial institution could undermine confidence, which could quickly ripple throughout markets. It called on policymakers to boost cybersecurity capacity, including stricter oversight of third-party technology vendors.
The IMF said its stress test models showed banks' capital cushions remained robust even in a hypothetical downturn triggered by an AI slowdown and bond market fragility. But it warned of "pockets of weakness," with banks representing 22% of global banking assets found to have "weak" capital levels under the test, up from 18% under the 2025 test.

items.author: ロイター

items.summary:
Rae Wee

items.body:
ＡＩがアジアの労働力減補う可能性　偏りない導入が前提＝ＩＭＦ
12:18 配信

国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事。１０月１２日、タイのバンコクで撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Athit Perawongmetha）

Rae Wee

[バンコク １２日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１２日、アジアで人工知能（ＡＩ）の導入が既存の格差を深めることなく均等に拡大すれば、一部で進む高齢化に伴う労働力減少を補う可能性があるとの見方を示した。

ＩＭＦのゲオルギエワ専務理事は、アジアの課題と機会を扱ったＩＭＦ書籍の発表会で、同地域が直面する３つの大きな「変革」として人口動態、経済統合、ＡＩを中心とする技術を挙げた。

同氏は「高齢化が進むアジアの先進国・地域では、ＡＩが成長率を０．５─１％ポイント押し上げると予想される。注目すべきは、各国がこうした生産性向上と成長を実現すれば、人口動態による下押し圧力を十二分に相殺することだ」と述べた。

ただ、ＩＭＦのクリシュナ・スリニバサン・アジア太平洋局長は、政策担当者はＡＩ導入の恩恵と、アジア各国間の格差拡大リスクを比較衡量する必要があると指摘。

バンコクで行われたＩＭＦ・世界銀行年次総会の一環で開かれた発表会で「重要なのは、ＡＩが労働者の能力を向上させるのか、仕事を自動化するのかという点だ。先進国は確実に影響を受けやすいが、恩恵を得る態勢もより整っている。新興国は影響を受けにくい一方、恩恵を取り込む態勢も十分でない」と述べた。

また「技能と生産性を高める改革が行われれば導入が１０年以上前倒しでき、これは明るい材料だ」と述べた。

items.summary: [１２日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックは１２日、同社のＡＩモデル「クロード」の能力を競合他...
items.body:
アンソロピックがＡＩ「蒸留」対策、データ抽出9割超減
12:13 配信

９月１７日、米カリフォルニア州サンフランシスコで撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Carlos Barria）

[１２日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックは１２日、同社のＡＩモデル「クロード」の能力を競合他社が模倣するのを防ぐために導入した新たな対策により、いわゆる「蒸留攻撃」で収集されるデータが約９０─９９％減少したと明らかにした。

• 米中の競争が激化する中、モデルの蒸留は主要ＡＩ企業にとって大きな懸念となっている。アンソロピックやオープンＡＩ、グーグルなどは、この手法によって競合他社が高度な能力をより短期間かつ低コストで再現できると主張している。

• アンソロピックによると、クロードの推論へのアクセスを制限する安全策により、データ抽出の試みは大幅に減少した。「蒸留を行う者によって抽出される推論トークンの数」は現在、「以前の１０分の１から１００分の１の水準」になったという。

• プロキシネットワークを使ってクロードの保護された推論を繰り返し探ることを一段と困難にし、抽出の試みを阻止するとともに、大規模な蒸留活動を妨げていると説明した。

• 同社はこの安全システムについて「クロードが生物兵器の製造を支援するのを防ぐ仕組みとほぼ同程度に堅牢」で、「誤検知率は０．１％未満」としている。

• 同社は蒸留活動に関連する数万件のアカウントを利用禁止にした。また、クロードの能力の蒸留を試みた企業の例として、中国の新興ＡＩ企業、智譜（Ｚ．ＡＩ）を挙げ、同社がモデル「ＧＬＭ─５．３」の開発中にこうした行為を試みたと指摘。安全性や国家安全保障上のリスクをもたらすと警告した。

items.title: 米クローガー、3年で3000人削減へ　ＡＩ導入で業務効率化
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [１２日 ロイター] - 米食品スーパー大手クローガーは、今後３年間にコーポレート部門で約３０００人を削減する方針。グ...
items.body:
米クローガー、3年で3000人削減へ　ＡＩ導入で業務効率化
12:12 配信

2025年2月11日撮影のイラスト。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[１２日 ロイター] - 米食品スーパー大手クローガーは、今後３年間にコーポレート部門で約３０００人を削減する方針。グレッグ・フォラン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が従業員向け文書で明らかにした。同社は業務への人工知能（ＡＩ）導入を進めている。

ロイターが１２日に確認した文書で、フォラン氏は、重複業務を減らして技術の進歩に対応すべきだと指摘。今回の人員削減は値下げや店舗従業員への投資につながると述べた。

コーポレート部門従業員８２００人の約３７％が影響を受けるという。フォラン氏は、数カ月以内に詳細を伝えるとした。同社は２０２５年６月にもコーポレート部門で約１０００人を削減している。

各社は業務効率化に向けてＡＩの活用を拡大し、ＡＩにより多くの経営資源を振り向ける中で、組織構造の見直しや人員削減を進めている。こうした動きは、業種を超えて広範囲な混乱が生じるとの懸念を強めている。

クローガーは９月にＡＩ戦略の概要を公表。これにはＡＩモデルによる業務管理や、顧客データを活用したＡＩ買い物アシスタントなどのツールの機能強化が含まれた。

また、９月に第２・四半期決算を発表した際、通期既存店売上高目標を引き下げた。ガソリン価格高騰で消費者が節約志向を強める中、ウォルマートやアルディなどの競合に対する競争力強化に向け値下げを目指していると説明した。

items.body:
午前の日経平均は大幅続落、ＡＩ・半導体株安が重し　循環物色も意識
12:10 配信

2026年9月23日撮影のイラスト。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Noriyuki Hirata

[東京 １３日 ロイター] - 前場の東京株式市場で日経平均は大幅に続落し、前営業日比２．５２％（１７３８円５３銭）安の６万７２９２円３９銭となった。米国市場での半導体株安が国内の人工知能（ＡＩ）・半導体関連株に波及し、指数の重しになった。一方、原油価格や金利が高止まりする中、石油関連株や金融株はしっかり。東証プライム市場の７割近い銘柄は値上がりし、循環物色も意識された。

・日経平均は一時２．８％（１９７２円）安の６万７０５８円に下げ拡大。マイナス寄与上位にはＡＩ関連株が並ぶ。

・アドバンテストとソフトバンクグループ、東京エレクトロンの３銘柄で指数を１２００円程度下押し。

・原油高でインフレ、金利高への懸念がくすぶる中、鉱業や石油・石炭製品、銀行、保険はしっかり。

・東証プライム市場の７割弱の銘柄が値上がり。９月来のハイテク株急上昇の裏で売られた銘柄群に物色との見方。

・ＴＯＰＩＸは０．４６％安の４０８５．９１ポイントで午前の取引を終了。

・日経平均に比べＴＯＰＩＸの下落率は限定的。ＮＴ倍率は１６．４倍台に急低下。

・東証プライム市場の売買代金は４兆０１５６億２４００万円。

・東証３３業種で上昇したのは、海運、証券、保険など２５業種、下落は非鉄金属、電気機器、金属製品など８業種。

・東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが１０６６銘柄（６８％）、値下がりは４５７銘柄（２９％）、変わらずは２９銘柄（１％）。

＜りそなアセットマネジメント シニアファンドマネージャー 戸田浩司氏＞

「（９月後半の）ハイテク株高はさしたる理由もなく、日経平均は７万円到達で利益確定売りに違和感なし」

「（９月のハイテク株高は）四半期、半期末を控えたセクター需給の偏りが背景か。一巡したことで循環物色に」

「さして売る材料も見当たらず、一巡すれば株価は戻りを想定」

「不透明感が残る中、楽観と悲観が循環。逆張りで対応する局面か」

items.title: Wild make first-period flurry hold up in win over Golden Knights
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Danila Yurov scored to finish off a first-period flurry for the Minnesota Wild, who held on for a 4-2 win over the Vegas Golden Knights on Monday evening in Saint Paul, Minn.
items.body:
Danila Yurov scored to finish off a first-period flurry for the Minnesota Wild, who held on for a 4-2 win over the Vegas Golden Knights on Monday evening in Saint Paul, Minn.
Matt Boldy and Maxim Shabanov also scored in the first period for Minnesota, which won its second game in a row. Joel Eriksson Ek added an empty-net goal.
Rasmus Andersson and William Karlsson scored one goal apiece for Vegas, which never led. The Golden Knights lost for the first time in their past five games.
Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt stopped 21 of 23 shots in the win.
Golden Knights goaltender Carter Hart allowed three goals on 27 shots.
The Wild opened the scoring with 8:10 to go in the first period. Boldy blasted a one-timer that Hart denied, but the rebound came back to Boldy's stick, leading to a successful second-chance snap shot.
Less than three minutes later, Shabanov scored on the power play to increase the Wild's advantage to 2-0. Shabanov fired a wrist shot from the top of the left circle, and the puck hit off Hart's blocker and ricocheted into the net.
Minnesota made it 3-0 two-plus minutes after that, which concluded a three-goal stretch within 5:07 in the back half of the first period. Bobby Brink zipped a pinpoint pass to the slot for Yurov, who buried a one-timer.
Vegas got on the scoreboard with 17:23 left in the second period. Andersson steadied the puck and fired a long-range slap shot from near the blue line for his first goal.
The Golden Knights cut the deficit to 3-2 with 10:35 remaining in the third period. On a two-on-one rush, Brett Howden flipped a saucer pass to Karlsson, who finished the job with a one-timer.
Vegas pulled its goaltender for an extra attacker in the final two minutes, but Minnesota held firm. Eriksson Ek scored an empty-net goal to make it 4-2 with 1:22 to go.
Wild forward Nico Sturm left the game in the first period and did not return after taking a puck to the right side of his head. Sturm was battling for position near the net when a teammate's wrist shot struck him near the helmet.
--Field Level Media

items.title: India's widened FX curbs, RBI intervention lift rupee to one-month peak
items.author: Jaspreet Kalra
items.creator: Jaspreet Kalra
items.summary: The Indian rupee rose to its strongest level in a month on Tuesday, hoisted by fresh central bank measures to alleviate pressure on the Asian currency and likely spot market intervention that magnified their impact.
items.body:
The Indian rupee rose to its strongest level in a month on Tuesday, hoisted by [USN:L4N45Z04K TEXT:"fresh central bank measures"] to alleviate pressure on the Asian currency and likely spot market intervention that magnified their impact.
The rupee rose to 95.0725 in early trading, the highest since early September, before paring gains to trade higher by 0.5% at 95.25 per dollar.
The Reserve Bank of India on Monday widened the scope of a recent cash deposit mandate for FX hedges to cover all transactions by banks, including hedging of the lenders' assets and liabilities.
This was the latest in a slew of steps since Saturday aimed at supporting the rupee, which last week tested record lows amid pressure from high oil prices and capital outflows.
The latest change, however, has [USN:L4N45Z09Q TEXT:"sowed confusion"] among bankers and prompted some of them to stop quoting dollar-rupee forwards in the interbank market.
Multiple bankers characterised the morning trading as "nervous," following the salvo of regulatory steps.
State-run banks, meanwhile, were spotted offering dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, traders said.
"The repeated rejection of 96.70–96.90 suggests that the dollar is facing a significant ceiling. With the RBI’s measures supporting the rupee, we expect USD/INR to move towards 95.00–94.80 in the near term," said Amit Pabari, managing director at FX advisory firm CR Forex in Mumbai.
The dollar-rupee forward market saw sharp swings with far-tenor premiums moving between gains and losses. Traders also pointed to sharp moves in the non-deliverable forward market.
The USD/INR 1-year forward implied yield, for instance, swung between 3.62% and 4.02% against 3.83% at the previous close.

items.title: AI boom bolstered growth in global trade,  benefiting China and India, IMF says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The strong demand for AI has bolstered growth in China, India and other Asian countries and outpaced the overall growth in global trade, the IMF's new chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said on Tuesday.
items.body:
The strong demand for AI has bolstered growth in China, India and other Asian countries and outpaced the overall growth in global trade, the IMF's new chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said on Tuesday.
Global trade would have grown at a far slower rate without the AI boost, Tenreyro told reporters at the annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok.
A long-time professor at the London School of Economics, [USN:FWN4390JA TEXT:"Tenreyro started her new job"] at the IMF in August.
Tenreyro said the IMF remained concerned about high debt levels, urging countries to start cutting budgets to reduce deficits. She said central bankers should pursue more restrictive policies, including raising interest rates to get inflation rates back to target.
Tenreyro said the AI-related boom in investment and trade had been a key driver of global growth, but AI supply chains were highly concentrated in a few countries and sectors, which created potential chokepoints.
Global trade grew 8.3% between 2023 and 2025, while global trade in AI grew by 29%, she said. Without the AI trade, overall growth in trade would have been only 4.6%.
The IMF flagged that a market value correction and AI threats to cybersecurity could also weigh on growth and add to financial stability risks. Tenreyro said the IMF's baseline forecast assumed the AI boom would dissipate over time, but another scenario showed that actual productivity gains from a prolonged AI boom could limit its inflationary impact.
If the AI boom persisted but did not result in productivity gains, the gains for growth would be smaller and inflation would be higher, she said. And a reassessment of the profitability gains from AI would result in downward adjustment in demand.
"It's basically an unwind of this boom that we are seeing," Tenreyro said, adding that the IMF was updating its research on the impact of AI on jobs.

items.summary: [１２日 ロイター] - 中国の人工知能（ＡＩ）新興企業ムーンショットＡＩ（月之暗面）の経営幹部らが、香港市場での新規株...
items.body:
ムーンショット幹部、香港ＩＰＯ控え株主との紛争解決へ協議＝関係筋
11:33 配信

写真はムーンショットＡＩのロゴ。2026年9月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[１２日 ロイター] - 中国の人工知能（ＡＩ）新興企業ムーンショットＡＩ（月之暗面）の経営幹部らが、香港市場での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）計画を前に、株主との法的紛争の解決に向けて協議していると、事情に詳しい複数の関係者が明らかにした。株主側は幹部らに不正行為があったとして補償を求めている。

ロイターが確認した３月１１日付の書簡によると、ＡＩソフトウエア開発企業リカレントＡＩとその一部投資家は、ムーンショットのヤン・ジーリン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）とチャン・ユータオ最高技術責任者（ＣＴＯ）が、リカレントの投資家に虚偽の説明をし、リカレントを犠牲にして個人的な利益を得たと主張している。書簡はリカレントの弁護士らがムーンショットの投資家に送ったもの。

企業登記によると、ヤン氏とチャン氏は２０１６年にリカレントを共同創業した後、２３年にムーンショットを設立した。両氏は現在もリカレントの持ち株会社の取締役を務めている。和解協議について報じられるのは初めて。

ロイターは書簡の主張の正確性を独自に確認できなかった。書簡にはリカレントの投資家の名前は記されていない。

ヤン氏とチャン氏は電子メールでのコメント要請に回答しなかった。ヤン氏は以前、疑惑を否定している。ムーンショットはコメントを控えた。

両氏とムーンショットの代理人を務める法律事務所ミンターエリソンのシニアパートナー、デービッド・モリソン氏は２４年１１月、中国メディアに対し、この申し立ては「法的根拠も事実関係上の根拠も欠いている」と述べ、争う方針を示した。

ロイターは、チャン氏が疑惑について公にコメントしたことがあるかどうか確認できなかった。

リカレントは電子メールでのコメント要請に回答しなかった。

リカレントはムーンショットの設立時に、当初の株式の９．５％を取得した。関係者の１人によると、リカレントとその投資家は、ムーンショットの当初の株式の１０．５％に相当する補償を求めている。６月の資金調達時の企業評価額３００億ドルに基づくと、補償額は７億ドルを超える可能性があるという。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Padmanabhan Ananthan

[１２日 ロイター] - 米製薬大手ブリストル・マイヤーズ・スクイブは１２日...
items.body:
米ブリストル肺疾患薬、後期試験で2用量のうち低用量に効果
11:31 配信

写真はブリストル・マイヤーズ・スクイブのロゴ。2021年5月、米マサチューセッツ州ケンブリッジで撮影。REUTERS/Brian Snyder

Padmanabhan Ananthan

[１２日 ロイター] - 米製薬大手ブリストル・マイヤーズ・スクイブは１２日、開発中の特発性肺線維症（ＩＰＦ）治療薬「アドミルパラント」について、後期臨床試験ではより低用量（６０ミリグラム）の投与によって病状の進行が抑制されたと発表した。承認されれば、ＩＰＦ治療薬として初のＬＰＡ１阻害剤となる見通しだ。

患者１２５５人が参加した試験で、ＬＰＡ１タンパク質受容体を阻害することで肺の線維化に関わる経路を標的とする同薬について２つの経口投薬量を検証した。

ブリストル・マイヤーズによると、１日２回６０ミリグラム投与群は５２週間後の肺機能維持で、プラセボ(偽薬)群を上回る効果を示した。しかしより高用量の１２０ミリグラム投与群では、試験の主要評価項目を達成できなかった。

アナリストらは安全性の懸念を理由に結果への期待を控えめにしていたとし、同薬の商業的可能性を評価するためには完全なデータが必要だと指摘した。

ただウィリアム・ブレアのアナリスト、マット・フィリップス氏は、６０ミリグラム用量の成功がブロックバスター（大型新薬）となる可能性を示すとし、２０３２年の売上高を約１３億ドルと推計した。

現在ＩＰＦの治療薬には、独同業のベーリンガーインゲルハイムの「オフェブ」と「ジャスケイド」、スイス同業のロシュの「エスブリエット」が含まれる。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Karen Freifeld　Jaspreet Singh

[ニューヨーク ９日 ロイター] - サーバー製造の米スー...
items.body:
スーパー・マイクロ請負業者、ＡＩサーバー不正輸出で有罪認める
11:28 配信

写真はスーパー・マイクロ・コンピューターのロゴ。2026年6月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Karen Freifeld　Jaspreet Singh

[ニューヨーク ９日 ロイター] - サーバー製造の米スーパー・マイクロ・コンピューターと関係のある請負業者が、エヌビディアの先端人工知能（ＡＩ）チップを搭載したコンピューターサーバーを中国へ違法に輸出するための計画に関連した罪を認めた。９日に公開された連邦裁判所資料で明らかになった。

ティンウェイ・「ウィリー」・スン被告は８日にマンハッタンの地裁で行われた罪状認否で、米国の輸出規制違反、米国からの物品密輸、国家に対する詐欺、司法妨害の共謀を含む４つの罪状について有罪を認めた。

検察当局は３月、スン被告のほか、スーパー・マイクロの共同創業者を含む同社関係者２人について、輸出関連法に違反して約２５億ドル相当の米ＡＩ技術を中国へ横流しするために共謀した罪で起訴した。

スーパー・マイクロはコメント要請に対し、同社は被告となっておらず、事業運営にも影響はないとするこれまでの声明に言及した。同社は今年、スン被告との契約を打ち切り、他の被告らとの関係も断っている。

スン被告の弁護士はコメントを控えた。

起訴状によると、同被告は仲介業者で、「フィクサー」として注文をあっせんし、この計画を隠蔽（いんぺい）するための措置を講じていたとされる。

items.title: 世界経済成長率予測、今年3.1％に上げ　ＡＩ投資堅調＝ＩＭＦ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
David Lawder

[バンコク １３日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１３日、２０２６年の世界経済成長...
items.body:
世界経済成長率予測、今年3.1％に上げ　ＡＩ投資堅調＝ＩＭＦ
11:24 配信

写真はIMFのロゴ。2024年11月、米ワシントンで撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

David Lawder

[バンコク １３日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１３日、２０２６年の世界経済成長率が３．１％になるとの見通しを示し、７月時点の予測値３．０％から上方修正した。堅調なＡＩ（人工知能）関連投資が中東戦争に伴うエネルギーショックを相殺するとしつつ、下振れリスクが高まっているとも警告した。

「世界経済見通し」の予測は、４月に示された最も楽観的なシナリオとほぼ同水準だが、２５年の世界経済成長率３．５％からは減速する。

２７年については３．４％と予測しており、これは７月時点からは変わらず、４月の予測からは０．２ポイント上方修正された。

今回の小幅な上方修正は、ＡＩプラットフォームを構築する主要先進国や、特に韓国、マレーシア、メキシコ、タイを含め、ＡＩハードウエアを供給する国々の成長見通しが上方修正されたことが要因となっている。

ＩＭＦの新チーフエコノミスト、シルバナ・テンレイロ氏は記者団に「世界経済は強靭性を示してきたが、その強靱性も限界に近づいており、単に対処する段階から、再構築する段階に移る必要がある」と指摘。「財政余力を回復する必要がある。供給面の強靱性を再構築する必要がある」と述べた。 

成長に対する主な下振れリスクとして、中東戦争の長期化・激化によるインフレ圧力の高まり、国債利回り上昇による政府借入コストの増大、エルニーニョ現象による異常気象、ＡＩ収益性の再評価による投資・資産価格の急落を挙げた。 

ＩＭＦ調査局のペティア・コエバ・ブルックス副局長はロイターとのインタビューで、各国や企業は原油価格ショックを緩和するため、備蓄の取り崩し、他の供給元やエネルギー源への切り替え、石油需要の削減といった措置を迅速に講じたと指摘。こうした措置がなければ今年の世界の成長率は２．５％まで低下していたはずだが、戦争が長期化するにつれてその効果は薄れつつあると語った。

ＩＭＦはまた、ＡＩの恩恵を受ける国々と、その恩恵を受けられない国々との間の格差が拡大していることに言及。現在、世界全体の成長の９５％を占めるのはわずか３２カ国で、４月時点では５４カ国だった。

イラン戦争の直接的な影響を受けた湾岸諸国には下方修正が広がっており、サウジアラビアの今年のＧＤＰ（国内総生産）は、７月に予測された１．７％のプラス成長から、３．３％のマイナス成長へと見直された。

イラン、イラク、クウェート、カタール、アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）も深刻な景気後退に陥ると予想されており、２６年のＧＤＰはそれぞれ７．６％、１６％、１６．７％、１５．６％、３．９％の縮小となる見込みだ。

＜米国は横ばい、欧州は改善＞

主要経済を見ると、ＩＭＦは米国の２６年および２７年の成長率をいずれも２．３％と予測。今年は据え置き、来年は０．１ポイント上方修正された。米国経済は、堅調な民間消費、減税、ＡＩ投資によって支えられると見込まれるが、ＡＩによる押し上げ効果は、その輸入依存度の高さによって相殺されそうだ。

ユーロ圏の２６年の成長率見通しは、ＡＩへの投資拡大、ドイツの化学製品生産などＡＩバリューチェーンへの参画、ＥＵ（欧州連合）諸国における防衛費の増加を背景に、７月時点の０．９％から１．１％へと上方修正された。英国の見通しも、７月時点から０．３ポイント上方修正され、１．３％となった。

中国の成長率は２６年が４．５％、２７年が４．０％となる見込み。いずれも７月時点の予測から０．１ポイント下方修正された。輸出は堅調であるものの、原油価格の上昇が国内需要の低迷をさらに悪化させているため。

インドは、堅調な内需、サービス業の活動、ＡＩ投資を背景に、２６年と２７年ともに７．０％の成長率を維持し、世界でもっとも成長の速い主要経済国であり続ける見通し。７月の予測と比較して、今年は０．６ポイント、来年は０．３ポイントの上方修正となる。

ＡＩ投資の急増は物価に上昇圧力をかけ続けると見込まれており、世界の総合消費者物価上昇率は２６年に４．７％、２７年に４．１％になると予測されている。

ＩＭＦはまた、特に先進国における公的債務水準の高さが、借入コストの急上昇リスクを高め、成長見通しに重くのしかかる恐れがあると警告。各国政府に対し、財政バッファーを再構築するための措置を先送りすることをやめ、債務を持続可能な水準に戻すための信頼性の高い中期計画を明確に示すよう強く求めた。

items.title: Gold ticks up as oil eases; spotlight on US inflation data
items.author: Ashitha Shivaprasad
items.creator: Ashitha Shivaprasad
items.summary: Gold ticked up on Tuesday as oil prices slipped, while markets focused on the upcoming US inflation data for fresh signals on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory.
items.body:
Gold ticked up on Tuesday as oil prices slipped, while markets focused on the upcoming US inflation data for fresh signals on the Federal Reserve's interest-rate trajectory.
Spot gold was up 0.4% to $4,188.27 per ounce by 06:24 GMT after hitting a one-week peak on Monday.
US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.5% to $4,212.50 per ounce.
Oil prices fell and were on track for their first decline in nearly a week.
Higher oil prices, driven by Middle East tensions, have raised inflation concerns and strengthened the case for restrictive monetary policy. While gold is considered a hedge against inflation, higher rates often push investors toward yield-bearing assets rather than the non-yielding metal.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is due on Wednesday, and the Producer Price Index (PPI) report is scheduled for Thursday.
"US CPI data will be critical for gold in the short term," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.
If inflation comes in hotter than expected, particularly on the core measure, and prompts even a modest increase in expectations of an October rate hike, it could result in another dip in gold, he added.
Currently, traders see only a 19% chance of a Fed rate hike this month but are pricing in an 85% chance of a December increase, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Cleveland Fed President [USN:S0N44V02D TEXT:"Beth Hammack"] said the US central bank should move "relatively quickly" to a more restrictive monetary policy stance to control inflation, which she feels has become broader-based and is starting to influence firms' price-setting plans.
On the geopolitical front, [USN:L6N45Y0OR TEXT:"Saudi Arabia"] said it was facing a new barrage of incoming fire and that Riyadh airport would remain shut for now, days after Saturday's deadly missile strike on a departure terminal that was claimed by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis.
Among other metals, spot silver gained 0.2% to $60.46 per ounce, platinum 0.5% to $1,694.65, and palladium fell 0.2% to $1,141.23 per ounce.

IMF cuts Latin America, Caribbean growth forecasts on energy shock, little AI boost

International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva speaks during the IMF/World Bank 2026 Annual Meetings at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok, Thailand, on Oct 12, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Athit Perawongmetha)

FAST

NEW YORK: The International Monetary Fund trimmed its growth forecasts for Latin America and the Caribbean for this year and next and said most of the region was getting little lift from the artificial intelligence boom that has helped other economies absorb the energy shock from the Middle East war.
In its World Economic Outlook, released early on Tuesday (Oct 13) in Bangkok, the Fund projected regional growth of 2.3 per cent this year. That is down from 2.5 per cent growth in 2025 and from its July forecast of 2.4 per cent growth for 2026. The IMF cut its 2027 forecast to 2.5 per cent from 2.7 per cent.
The regional downgrades come even as the Fund nudged up its world growth forecast for this year to 3.1 per cent from July's 3.0 per cent, crediting rerouted energy supplies and AI-driven investment for the resilience of what it calls a split global economy.
The Middle East war has turned energy into a global inflation shock, with Brent crude about 45 per cent above its prewar level. Higher fuel and power costs are squeezing households and businesses, while fears of persistent inflation have helped push global borrowing costs to multidecade highs.

In Latin America, the IMF said, the energy shock's effect depends on whether gains for commodity exporters outweigh losses for energy importers and on how credible central banks' inflation targets are, adding that "there is little offset from the technology upturn in most countries."
Of the three Latin American economies the IMF listed separately in its July World Economic Outlook update, Argentina took the deepest cut in its output estimate. The Fund now expects Argentine growth to slow to 2.1 per cent this year from 4.5 per cent in 2025, well below the 3.5 per cent it forecast in July, and it lowered its 2027 forecast to 3.5 per cent from 4.0 per cent. The report shows inflation is forecast to fall to 32.5 per cent this year from 41.9 per cent in 2025.
Brazil's forecasts fell to 2.2 per cent for this year and 1.9 per cent for 2027, from 2.4 per cent and 2.2 per cent in July, when the IMF had expected Brazilian growth to "remain resilient" this year. The Fund now expects growth to slow next year, citing still-restrictive monetary conditions aimed at bringing inflation back to target, the withdrawal of government fiscal support and global uncertainty.
Mexico moved the other way, with its 2026 forecast raised to 1.5 per cent from 1.2 per cent. The Fund previously linked Mexico's expected pickup to less restrictive domestic policies. It now points to exports, including through AI supply chains, and to investment that is stabilising as growth quickens next year. Even so, it trimmed Mexico's 2027 forecast to 1.8 per cent from 1.9 per cent and said trade and other uncertainties would keep holding back activity.
The report's tables show Chile's growth slowing to 0.6 per cent this year from 2.5 per cent, Bolivia's economy shrinking 3.0 per cent after a 1.6 per cent contraction in 2025, and Venezuelan inflation speeding up to 467.9 per cent from 252.0 per cent.
The IMF said risks remain tilted to the downside. It warned that market turmoil could hit emerging economies through higher government borrowing costs, pressure on their currencies and tighter local financial conditions.

Source: Reuters

items.title: 日銀、中立水準に段階的利上げへ　成長減速見通しでも＝ＩＭＦ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Leika Kihara

[１３日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１３日、日本の成長率は減速が予想されるもの...
items.body:
日銀、中立水準に段階的利上げへ　成長減速見通しでも＝ＩＭＦ
11:07 配信

写真は日本銀行本店。2026年9月18日、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Leika Kihara

[１３日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１３日、日本の成長率は減速が予想されるものの、日銀は金利を「中立的な水準に向けて」段階的に引き上げる可能性が高いとの見方を示した。インフレ圧力に直面する他の中央銀行と足並みをそろえる形となる。

ＩＭＦは世界経済見通しで「日本の成長率は２０２６年に０．７％に減速する見通しで、財政支援策がエネルギー価格上昇の影響を一部和らげる。２７年にはエネルギーショックが和らぎ、金融政策が徐々に正常化する中、成長率はこの水準で安定する見通しだ」と指摘した。

２５年の日本の成長率は１．２％だった。ＩＭＦは２７年についても０．７％の成長を予想している。

日銀は９月、政策金利を３１年ぶりの高水準となる１．２５％に引き上げた。また、インフレ率が２％の目標を超えて上振れするリスクを防ぐため、金融引き締めを継続する用意があることも示唆した。

日本は燃料や原材料を輸入に大きく依存しているため、エネルギーショックや通貨安によるインフレの影響を特に受けやすい。

ＩＭＦは特定の国を名指しせず、金融政策がインフレへの直接的な影響や短期的な間接影響を静観できるのは「ショックが一時的な場合に限られる」と指摘。

ショックを静観することが適切と判断される場合でも、インフレ期待が高まれば、中銀は実質的な借り入れコストを一定に保つため、名目金利を引き上げる必要が生じる可能性があるとした。

また、為替相場は特にアジアでボラティリティーが高まり、円を下支えするための日米共同介入を含め、一部の国が介入に動いたと言及した。

「大規模なショックが進行する中では、秩序ある調整と金融安定の維持が不可欠だ」とした。

ＩＭＦは、外的ショックを吸収するため各国は為替相場の柔軟な変動を容認すべきだとする一方、市場の動きが無秩序になった場合には為替介入が選択肢になるとの見解を示した。

「（通貨の）下落が自己強化的になったり、市場流動性が枯渇したり、あるいは為替変動が大幅な価格転嫁やバランスシートへの圧力を通じて物価安定を脅かす場合には、一時的な為替介入」が検討可能だとした。

items.title: AI investment props up global growth, but war and debt threaten outlook, IMF says
items.author: David Lawder
items.creator: David Lawder
items.summary: The global economy will still manage to top 3% real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East, but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday.
items.body:
The global economy will still manage to top 3% real GDP growth this year as strong AI investment offsets the energy shock from the war in the Middle East , but downside risks are mounting and more countries are being left behind and vulnerable to rising debt loads, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday.
Despite a more protracted conflict that has kept oil prices above $100 a barrel, the IMF is forecasting 2026 global growth at 3.1%, a slight uptick from the 3.0% it [USN:L1N43A0MP TEXT:"predicted in July"].
The [USN:L1N45Y0HP TEXT:"World Economic Outlook"] forecast, released as global economic and finance leaders gather in Bangkok for the [USN:L1N45X02O TEXT:"IMF and World Bank annual meetings"], is about even with the [USN:L1N40X0Q2 TEXT:"most optimistic scenario"] issued in April but below 2025 global growth of 3.5%.
For 2027, the IMF predicts 3.4% global growth, flat with the July forecast and up 0.2 percentage point from April.
The slight improvement is largely due to continued strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure, prompting growth upgrades for key advanced economies building AI platforms and especially for countries supplying AI hardware, including South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico and Thailand, which is hosting the meetings this week.
"The global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits, so we need to move from just coping to rebuilding," the IMF's chief economist, Silvana Tenreyro, told a news conference. "We need to restore fiscal space. We need to rebuild supply-side resilience."
She said major downside risks to growth include a prolonged, intensified war in the Middle East that spikes inflation pressures, rising bond yields that raise government borrowing costs, El Nino-driven extreme weather events and a reassessment of AI profitability that craters investment and asset prices.
Countries and companies moved quickly to mitigate the oil price shock, drawing down reserves, substituting other suppliers and energy sources and cutting oil demand, Petya Koeva Brooks, the IMF's deputy research director, told Reuters in a separate interview. She said global growth would have fallen to 2.5% this year without these measures, but their effect is fading as the war drags on.
The IMF noted a growing divergence between countries benefiting from AI and those bypassed by it. Just 32 countries now account for 95% of global growth, compared to 54 countries in April.
Downward growth revisions have become more widespread, with the IMF downgrading 47% of economies since the April forecasts were issued, including several energy importers outside AI value chains.
Hardest hit by downgrades were the Gulf countries directly impacted by the US-Israeli war against Iran, with Saudi Arabia's GDP now forecast to contract 3.3% this year compared with the 1.7% growth predicted in July.
Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates are also expected to fall into deep recessions, with 2026 contractions of 7.6%, 16%, 16.7%, 15.6% and 3.9%, respectively.
UNITED STATES FLAT, IMPROVEMENT IN EUROPE Among major economies, the IMF forecast US growth of 2.3% for both 2026 and 2027, unchanged for this year and 0.1 percentage point higher for next year. The US economy is expected to be supported by robust private consumption, tax cuts and AI investment, though the boost from AI will be offset by its large import content.
Euro zone growth for 2026 was upgraded to 1.1% from 0.9% in July due to stronger investment in AI, participation in AI value chains such as chemical production in Germany, and higher defense spending in EU countries. Britain's 2026 growth forecast also was upgraded by 0.3 percentage point from July to 1.3% due to larger AI investment.
The IMF forecast China's growth at 4.5% for 2026 and 4.0% for 2027, both down 0.1 percentage point from July, as higher oil prices exacerbate weak domestic demand despite strong exports.
India remains the world's fastest-growing major economy at 7.0% for both 2026 and 2027, up 0.6 percentage point this year and 0.3 percentage point next year compared with the July forecasts amid robust domestic demand, services activity and AI investment.
The AI investment surge is projected to keep upward pressure on prices, with global headline consumer price inflation forecast at 4.7% in 2026 and 4.1% for 2027.
ENERGY PRICE, AI RISKS Participants at the IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok will be assessing a precarious outlook. The IMF forecasts are based on assumptions that the Strait of Hormuz will reopen in March 2027 with a broad return to pre-war shipping conditions occurring by October 2027. The IMF assumes an average oil price of $96 per barrel for 2026 and $87 in 2027.
But under an adverse scenario highlighted in the report, in which a worsening war pushes oil prices to $130 per barrel through the first quarter of 2027, growth would be reduced by 0.2 percentage point in 2026 and 0.5 percentage point in 2027. Inflation in 2027 would surge by another 1.1 percentage point to 5.2%.
AI is also a huge source of uncertainty, with major downside and upside risks, the IMF report said. Under a scenario of faster adoption of the technology and accelerated investment, global GDP could rise a further 0.6% by 2029, with the bulk of the benefits going to the US and China.
But if productivity gains from AI fail to materialize, prompting a sharp decline in investment, US GDP could fall by 0.8% directly, causing spillovers to Asian technology exporters with a total direct GDP impact of as much as 0.4% by 2028.
This shift would also trigger a sharp reduction in asset prices and tighter financial conditions that cause a major drop in consumption, particularly in the US, the IMF said. Higher global bond yields would further reduce activity, with a combined global output reduction of 1.1% by 2028, including a 1.8% drop in US output.
The IMF also warned that elevated public debt levels, particularly in advanced economies, increase the risk of sharply higher borrowing costs that can weigh on growth prospects. It urged governments to stop delaying action to rebuild fiscal buffers and articulate credible medium-term plans to bring debt back to sustainable levels — advice that IMF officials [USN:L6N45T0FB TEXT:"plan to push"] at the Bangkok meetings.

IMF expects gradual BOJ rate hike towards neutral setting

FAST

The International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday (Oct 13) the Bank of Japan will likely raise interest rates gradually "toward a neutral setting" despite an expected slowdown in growth, aligning with other central banks facing inflationary pressures.
"Growth in Japan is projected to slow to 0.7 per cent in 2026, with fiscal support measures partly cushioning the impact from higher energy prices, and to stabilise at that level in 2027 as the energy shock dissipates and monetary policy gradually normalises," the IMF said in its World Economic Outlook.
The growth forecast for 2026 follows last year's 1.2 per cent expansion. The IMF expects Japan's economy to grow 0.7 per cent in 2027.
The BOJ raised interest rates to a 31-year high of 1.25 per cent in September and signalled its readiness to keep tightening policy to forestall the risk of inflation overshooting its 2 per cent target.

Japan's heavy reliance on imports for fuel and raw materials makes its economy particularly vulnerable to the inflationary impact from the energy shock and a weak currency.
Without singling out any country, the IMF said monetary policy can look through the direct and short-term indirect effects on inflation "only if the shock is temporary."
Even where looking through the shock is deemed appropriate, central banks may need to raise nominal interest rates if inflation expectations heighten, to keep real borrowing costs steady, it said in the report.
The report also said exchange rates have experienced high volatility especially in Asia, prompting intervention by some countries, including a joint Japan-US operation to prop up the sagging yen.
"Maintaining orderly adjustment and financial stability is vital while large shocks are unfolding," it said.
While economies should allow exchange rates to move flexibly to absorb external shocks, currency intervention becomes an option if market moves are disorderly, the IMF said.
"Where (currency) depreciation becomes self-reinforcing, market liquidity evaporates, or currency movements threaten price stability through large pass-through or balance sheet stress, temporary foreign exchange intervention" can be considered, the report said.

items.title: US says it opposes Chinese 'coercion', after Belize, Paraguay ministers sanctioned
items.author: Ben Blanchard
items.creator: Ben Blanchard
items.summary: The Trump administration opposes "coercion and aggression" by China against countries for exercising their sovereign rights, the US State Department said, after Beijing sanctioned Belizean and Paraguayan ministers over their ties to Taiwan.
items.body:
The Trump administration opposes "coercion and aggression" by China against countries for exercising their sovereign rights, the US State Department said, after Beijing [USN:L1N45Y01O TEXT:"sanctioned"] Belizean and Paraguayan ministers over their ties to Taiwan.
Paraguay and Belize are two of just 12 countries to maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan. China says Taiwan is one of its provinces with no right to behave like a state, a view Taipei's government strongly rejects.
The sanctions are largely symbolic because ministers from Taiwan's diplomatic allies generally do not travel to China. Beijing has previously imposed similar measures mainly on Western politicians for their support of democratically governed Taiwan.
"The Trump administration opposes coercion and aggression by China against countries in our hemisphere for exercising their sovereign rights," State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said in a statement.
Pigott cited previous comments by Secretary of State Marco Rubio that the US "will not allow our region to become a base of operation for adversaries, competitors, and rivals to threaten our security or undermine our partnerships".
"We stand with our friends and partners, including Taiwan, to advance our shared prosperity, security, and values," Pigott added.
A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said the United States should "stop sending the wrong signals to Taiwan separatist forces".
The United States is Taiwan's most important international backer, despite the lack of formal diplomatic ties.
Washington has been concerned not only by Beijing's efforts to win over Taiwan's remaining allies, but also by attempts to increase its influence in Latin America.
TAIWAN'S VISIBILITY 'GROWING HIGHER' Speaking on Tuesday to reporters at parliament in Taipei, Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi said China was extending "transnational repression" to Taiwan's allies.
"Taiwan's international visibility is growing higher and higher, and they will be kept busy by this fact," Chen said, referring to China. "Do they plan to sanction the whole world?"
Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai said Beijing had no right to interfere in the domestic affairs of, or influence the diplomacy of, any sovereign and independent state, "including the Republic of China", referring to the island's formal name.
"At the same time, we will resist any expansion of hegemony or authoritarianism," he added, also speaking at parliament.
China has stepped up pressure on Taiwan's remaining diplomatic allies to sever ties with Taipei.
The last country to do so was the tiny Pacific Island nation of Nauru, in 2024. Honduras ended its decades-long ties with Taiwan in 2023.

items.title: Linus Ullmark shines as Senators turn back Devils
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Linus Ullmark continued his early-season dominance to carry the Ottawa Senators to their third consecutive victory with a 4-1 win over the New Jersey Devils Monday night in Newark, N.J.
items.body:
Linus Ullmark continued his early-season dominance to carry the Ottawa Senators to their third consecutive victory with a 4-1 win over the New Jersey Devils Monday night in Newark, N.J.
Ullmark impressed with 29 saves to lift his record to a perfect 5-0-0 to start the season.
Tim Stutzle scored and picked up an assist, while Shane Pinto, Stephen Halliday and Tyler Kleven also lit the lamp for the Senators.
Arseny Gritsyuk tallied the Devils' lone goal and Nico Daws finished with 16 saves in the losing effort.
The Devils' physical play in the early going finally caught up to them as Anthony Mantha delivered a dangerous check on Nikolas Matinpalo that drew a five-minute major just over halfway through the opening frame.
Matinpalo was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the contest with an upper-body injury.
Fabian Zetterlund had the Senators' only real chance to score during their extended man advantage, but Daws slid across to deny the one-timer opportunity.
Ottawa started the second period off with a bang as Pinto found the back of the net just nine seconds in to give the Senators the 1-0 lead.
Michael Amadio picked up a pass from Claude Giroux and relayed it over to Pinto for his first goal of the season.
After failing to convert on their first four opportunities, the Senators finally found some power-play success as Stutzle spotted Halliday open in front of the net to double up the lead with 11:20 remaining in the second.
Stutzle picked up his 10th point of the season when he tipped Thomas Chabot's point shot past Daws to make it 3-0 with 8:50 left in the contest.
The Devils thought they finally got one past Ullmark less than a minute later, but it was ruled that Cody Glass illegally poked it loose from underneath the Senators' netminder following a successful coach's challenge.
Gritsyuk spoiled Ullmark's shutout bid as his shot passed through a screen and into the back of the net with just 5:01 remaining.
Kleven locked up the victory with an empty-net goal.
--Field Level Media

items.title: 中国テンセント、ドル建て債・点心債発行へ　ＡＩ投資拡大で資金確保目指す
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Yantoultra Ngui

[香港 １３日 ロイター] - 中国のゲーム・インターネット企業、騰訊控股（テンセント...
items.body:
中国テンセント、ドル建て債・点心債発行へ　ＡＩ投資拡大で資金確保目指す
10:48 配信

４月１７日、広東省深セン市で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Go Nakamura）

Yantoultra Ngui

[香港 １３日 ロイター] - 中国のゲーム・インターネット企業、騰訊控股（テンセント・ホールディングス）は、ドル建て債とオフショア人民元建て債（点心債）を発行し、少なくとも４５億ドルを調達する可能性がある。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連の支出が増える中、資金確保を目指す。 

ロイターが１３日に確認したタームシート（発行条件書）によると、発行するのは期間１０年と２０年のドル建て債、および期間１０年と３０年の点心債。各債券の発行額は明記されていない。

１０年物のドル建て債は、同年限の米国債利回りに対して約１１５ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上乗せ、２０年物については約１４０ｂｐ上乗せした水準を初期の利回りガイダンスとして設定した。

タームシートの最新情報によると、ドル建て債２本の応募額は２０億ドルを突破した。このうち５億２５００万ドルは共同主幹事からの購入意向だった。 

１０年物の点心債のガイダンスは約２．９０％、３０年物は３．５０％に設定した。

点心債の応募額は３５０億元（５２億ドル）を上回った。このうち２０２億５０００万元が共同主幹事からの注文で、６０００万元の自己勘定からの引き合いも含まれる。

テンセントはコメント要請に直ちに回答しなかった。

今回の起債計画は、テンセントがＡＩ関連のインフラや製品への投資を拡大する中で浮上した。

発行関連資料によると、同社の設備投資額は２０２６年上半期に９６３億元と、前年同期の４５９億元から倍以上に増加した。コンピューティング機器やソフトウエア、データセンターへの支出が含まれる。

タームシートによると、ドル建て債の共同グローバルコーディネーターは、ＪＰモルガン、ゴールドマン・サックス、ＨＳＢＣ、モルガン・スタンレーが務める。

点心債発行のコーディネーターは、中国工商銀行（アジア）、中国農業銀行、中国銀行、交通銀行、中国建設銀行、中信証券、ＨＳＢＣ、ＪＰモルガン。

items.title: Tencent experiences strong demand for $4.5 billion debt sale, defying AI scrutiny
items.author: Yantoultra Ngui, Ankur Banerjee
items.creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Ankur Banerjee
items.summary: Tencent Holdings has received investor demand worth more than three times the Chinese tech giant's plan to raise at least $4.5 billion via US dollar and offshore Chinese yuan debt offerings, even as AI spending jitters hit the global markets.
items.body:
Tencent Holdings (0700.HK) has received investor demand worth more than three times the Chinese tech giant's plan to raise at least $4.5 billion via US dollar and offshore Chinese yuan debt offerings, even as AI spending jitters hit the global markets.
Tencent plans to use the proceeds for general corporate purposes, according to the deal term sheet, and the latest borrowing comes as the company increases investment in AI infrastructure and products.
The latest debt sale comes amid technology firms globally [USN:L6N45F1AU TEXT:"raising billions of dollars"] to finance [USN:L1N455022 TEXT:"AI investment"]s, although investors have become [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"more selective about companies"] funding costly AI infrastructure amid elevated borrowing costs.
Shares in AI suppliers came under [USN:L1N45Z029 TEXT:"heavy selling pressure"] on Tuesday on growing concerns about competition risks in the sector and rising interest rates weighing on AI-related borrowing and a spending spree.
Despite those concerns, investor demand for Tencent's 10-year and 20-year US dollar notes topped $4 billion, including $921 million in interest from the joint lead managers, according to an updated term sheet issued on Tuesday.
Order books for the 10-year and 30-year offshore yuan, or dim sum, bonds exceeded 77 billion yuan ($11.5 billion), the sheet showed.
The total demand worth $15.5 billion is significantly higher than at least [USN:L4N45Y01K TEXT:"$4.5 billion"] that a person with direct knowledge of the deal told Reuters on Monday the company was looking to raise.
The company [USN:L1N42H00X TEXT:"last tapped the bond market in June"], raising about $4.66 billion through dollar- and yuan-denominated notes.
Its return to the bond market so quickly suggests capital remains available for AI, particularly for companies with strong cash flows, balance sheets and credible monetisation plans, said Allspring Global Investments portfolio manager Gary Tan.
"We are seeing a more definitive shift in sentiment around the pace of AI spending, as investors increasingly view financing availability and the cost of capital as potential bottlenecks to a further acceleration in AI investment," he said.
Tencent has not responded to a Reuters request seeking comment on its debt issuance. The deal term sheet did not specify how much the company is looking to raise via the sale of US dollar and offshore yuan notes.
CAPITAL EXPENDITURE DOUBLES Shares in Tencent were down 0.5% on Tuesday, underperforming the benchmark Hang Seng Index (.HSI) that climbed 0.1%. The Hang Seng Tech Index (.HSTECH) fell nearly 1%. Tencent's shares have fallen about 30% so far this year.
Tencent set initial guidance for the 10-year dollar notes at about 115 basis points over comparable US Treasury bonds. The 20-year notes were set at about 140 basis points over Treasuries, according to the term sheet.
It set initial yield guidance at around 2.90% for the 10-year offshore yuan notes and 3.50% for the 30-year notes, the sheets showed. The final coupons for all the bonds are expected to be determined later Tuesday, according to the sheets.
Tencent's capital expenditure more than doubled to 96.3 billion yuan in the first half of 2026 from 45.9 billion yuan a year earlier, according to its offering documents. The spending included computing equipment, software and data centres.
The bonds are expected to be rated A1 by Moody's and A+ by S&P. Tencent is rated A1 by Moody's, A+ by S&P and A by Fitch, according to the term sheet.
JPMorgan (JPM.N) , Goldman Sachs (GS.N) , HSBC (HSBA.L) and Morgan Stanley (MS.N) are joint global coordinators for Tencent's dollar bond offering, the sheet showed.
ICBC (Asia), Agricultural Bank of China, Bank of China, Bank of Communications, China Construction Bank, CITIC Securities, HSBC and JPMorgan are coordinating the offshore yuan sale, according to the sheet.
($1 = 6.6923 Chinese yuan renminbi)

items.body:
豪企業信頼感指数、9月にマイナス幅拡大　コスト上昇懸念高まる
10:14 配信

７月２日、オーストラリアのシドニーで撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Hollie Adams）

[シドニー １３日 ロイター] - ナショナル・オーストラリア銀行（ＮＡＢ）が１３日発表した９月の企業景況感指数は前月と同様マイナス１となったものの、中東情勢の再緊迫化による原油価格の高騰を背景に信頼感指数は４ポイント低下してマイナス１３となり、コスト上昇への懸念が高まっていることが明らかになった。

信頼感指数はイラン戦争が始まる前の２月に記録された水準を大幅に下回っている。

ＮＡＢは「２０２６年はエネルギー価格が高止まりしており、資金調達コストが上昇し、国内成長も鈍化している」と指摘。信頼感の低下により、景況感がさらに悪化する可能性が高いとしている。

前月と比べ、８産業のうち５産業で信頼感が低下。鉱業、卸売業、小売業ではセンチメントが「若干の改善」を見せたものの、トレンドとしては鉱業を除く全産業で信頼感がマイナスのままだという。

TOKYO, Oct 13 : Japanese manufacturer Omron will buy US industrial PC firm Onlogic and its parent company, Interlogic, for $675 million, the company said on Tuesday.
The acquisition is intended to develop Omron's physical artificial intelligence services within its industrial automation business, the company said in a news release.
• Onlogic is a developer, manufacturer and seller of industrial PCs, with which Omron hopes to combine its high-precision control technology to develop physical AI platforms and expand its customer base in the US.
• Onlogic's parent, Interlogic, will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Omron. Onlogic will continue to operate as an independent business, retaining its brand and current management team, the release said.

items.title: Chandrasekaran defends Tata's long-term bets despite near-term uncertainty
items.summary: At Bloomberg's New Economy Forum, Chandrasekaran defended chip investments and long-term capital allocation, even as differences with Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata deepen over leadership and listing ...
items.body:
Home / Companies / News / Chandrasekaran defends Tata's long-term bets despite near-term uncertainty

Chandrasekaran defends Tata's long-term bets despite near-term uncertainty At Bloomberg's New Economy Forum, Chandrasekaran defended chip investments and long-term capital allocation, even as differences with Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata deepen over leadership and listing

Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran (Photo:PTI)

Barkha Mathur New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 12:58 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran on Tuesday defended the conglomerate's long-term investment strategy, saying the group will keep building what India and the world needs even when the benefits were not immediately visible.
  Speaking at Bloomberg' s New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Chandrasekaran said semiconductor manufacturing and advanced manufacturing were critical to India's future and should not be judged solely by whether they meet targets over the next two to three years.
  "There are many decisions that have been taken by various chairmen in the group which have all proved to be right in the long term," he said.
  His comments come amid a growing rift between Tata Sons and its controlling shareholder, Tata Trusts , over the group's investment strategy, Chandrasekaran's own reappointment and whether the holding company should go public.
 

  In September, the Tata Sons board reappointed Chandrasekaran for another five-year term, despite opposition from Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts. The Trusts, which own about 66 per cent of Tata Sons, later termed the decision illegal, arguing that it violated the company's Articles of Association. Tata Sons has disputed this claim.   ALSO READ: Tata Trusts seeks more time to reply; Charity Commissioner grants a week  
Also Read

Delhi SIR: 2 million cases resolved after EC eases voter verification rules

US visa, green card applicants face new filing deadline rules from Oct 23

NHAI mandates independent design checks for bridges, tunnels from December

From Sudha Yadav to Dushyant Gautam, meet the six newly appointed governors

Why 7-Eleven's India ambitions faltered despite Reliance Retail partnership

  “Direction is certain, need is certain, ability to execute is certain,” Chandrasekaran said, referring to the group's semiconductor ambitions. “The only thing is how much you ramp up, how fast you ramp up, which technology you go to. All this is uncertain.”

  “Sometimes things go wrong. Then you course-correct,” he said, adding that investments should be directed towards what India, enterprises and society need over the long term.
  Chandrasekaran acknowledged that the group would need technology partners. He also cautioned against investing recklessly in advanced chip technologies without considering demand and the balance sheet.
  “You can't be reckless and say that I am going to be putting a two-nanometre chip. It's just not going to work,” he said.   According to Tata Sons’ disclosures, Tata Electronics’ revenue nearly doubled to ₹1.31 trillion in FY26, but its net loss widened to ₹1,611 crore from ₹70 crore a year earlier. Its two major semiconductor projects are yet to begin production. The chip fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat, being built with Taiwan’s Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation, is expected to begin commercial operations in mid-2028, while the assembly and testing facility in Assam is slated to start production in December.

Resilience as a business priority Chandrasekaran said businesses should build resilience into their operations instead of focusing solely on efficiency in an unpredictable environment. He argued that the two were not mutually exclusive.
  “In a highly unpredictable, volatile environment, optimising for efficiency is definitely not the right thing,” he said. “I believe that if you design for resilience in an unpredictable environment, actually you are optimising for efficiency.”
  He cited shortages of magnets that can disrupt vehicle production and the cyberattack that affected Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), saying the company had almost lost six weeks of production because of the incident.
  The group had also faced an air crash and supply-chain disruptions, he said, but still expected to deliver double-digit growth, with margins holding up. He did not specify the period or provide financial projections to quantify the outlook.

  Chandrasekaran said he had asked companies across the group to define resilience for their own businesses rather than adopt a single framework.
Geopolitical risks and technology Chandrasekaran said technology posed near-term risks, including misuse by bad actors and job restructuring, but expected it to have a far-reaching impact over the medium to long term.
  He also expressed concern over the growing number of conflicts around the world, warning that wars were opening on multiple fronts without any being resolved.
  "If you look at a group like ours, which is about 160 years old, we have seen two world wars, pandemics, high borrowing levels and many other things, and we have survived. So it's not the first time that something as hard as this is happening. But the primary difference is that all of it is happening at the same time. Tackling all of it at the same time is the unique thing now," he said.

items.title: Oil falls as Russian diesel supply prospects counter Gulf supply risks
items.author: Anjana Anil, Trixie Yap
items.creator: Anjana Anil, Trixie Yap
items.summary: Oil prices fell on Tuesday and were on track for their first decline in nearly a week, as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.
items.body:
Oil prices fell on Tuesday and were on track for their first decline in nearly a week, as traders assessed supply risks from attacks on Saudi Arabia while weighing the prospect of additional diesel supplies from Russia.
Brent crude futures dropped $1.18, or 1.1%, to $105.47 a barrel by 0625 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down $1.17, or 1.3%, at $92.57 a barrel.
Both benchmarks climbed nearly $2 a barrel in the previous session, with Brent settling at its highest since September 15.
US President Donald Trump said Russia had agreed to [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"supply diesel"] to global markets, and his administration temporarily lifted US sanctions on Russian fuel designed to deprive Moscow of revenue for its war on Ukraine .
Additional supplies could help alleviate tightness in global fuel markets, tempering some of the supply concerns that have supported crude prices recently.
However, "there is considerable scepticism over the Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, particularly with reports that Russia has hit Ukrainian energy targets since Trump announced it," ING analysts said in a note.
Lawmakers from both parties in the US complained Trump's agreement with Putin appears to [USN:L1N45Y0QE TEXT:"violate US law"] barring imports of Russian energy until Moscow ends its aggression against Ukraine.
Concerns over the vulnerability of Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping lanes remained in focus after Iran-aligned Houthis [USN:L6N45Y0C1 TEXT:"struck Riyadh's international airport"] over the weekend, while [USN:L1N45T0HL TEXT:"tanker attacks"] were [USN:S8N44X01M TEXT:"reported"] near the Strait of Hormuz.
The incidents threatened to derail a recovery in Middle East supplies seen in September, and have reinforced fears of further disruptions along one of the world's most important energy transit routes.
"Fresh diesel supply from Russia and steadier Saudi flows are offering some relief, yet the market still looks more worried about the risk of further hits to ships or pipelines in the Gulf than it is reassured by extra barrels," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.
"Until we see clearer signs of de-escalation, the path of least resistance still leans higher," he said.
Ministers of OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the Declaration of Cooperation said shipping and insurance costs have surged to unprecedented levels of over [USN:L4N45Y17D TEXT:"one-third"] of the commodity value, impeding efficient movement of crude oil and products.
OPEC has [USN:S8N45M04R TEXT:"revised down"] its oil demand growth forecast for this year to 400,000 barrels per day from 1.4 million bpd at the start of the year, in line with developments throughout the year, Haitham Al Ghais, Secretary General of the organisation said on Monday.

Lawmakers from both parties in the US complained Trump's agreement with Putin appears to violate US law barring imports of Russian energy until Moscow ends its aggression against Ukraine.
Concerns over the vulnerability of Gulf energy infrastructure and shipping lanes remained in focus after Iran-aligned Houthis struck Riyadh's international airport over the weekend, while tanker attacks were reported near the Strait of Hormuz.
The incidents threatened to derail a recovery in Middle East supplies seen in September, and have reinforced fears of further disruptions along one of the world's most important energy transit routes.
"Fresh diesel supply from Russia and steadier Saudi flows are offering some relief, yet the market still looks more worried about the risk of further hits to ships or pipelines in the Gulf than it is reassured by extra barrels," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.
"Until we see clearer signs of de-escalation, the path of least resistance still leans higher," he said.
Ministers of OPEC and non-OPEC Participating Countries in the Declaration of Cooperation said shipping and insurance costs have surged to unprecedented levels of over one-third of the commodity value, impeding efficient movement of crude oil and products.
OPEC has revised down its oil demand growth forecast for this year to 400,000 barrels per day from 1.4 million bpd at the start of the year, in line with developments throughout the year, Haitham Al Ghais, Secretary General of the organisation said on Monday.

RJ Mitte, Breaking Bad actor and disability rights advocate, dies at 34

RJ Mitte rose to fame playing Walter White Jr in the acclaimed television series Breaking Bad. He drew on his personal experience with cerebral palsy to portray the character.

Actor RJ Mitte poses at the premiere for 'El Camino: A Breaking Bad Movie' in Los Angeles, California, U.S., October 7, 2019. REUTERS/Mario Anzuoni/File Photo

FAST

Actor RJ Mitte, whose personal experience living with cerebral palsy informed his role as Walter White Jr, the physically disabled son of a methamphetamine kingpin in the landmark television show Breaking Bad, died on Monday (Oct 12) at age 34.
News of Mitte's death in Brownsville, Texas, was confirmed in a statement released through the talent management agency that represented the actor. No other details about the circumstances of his death were given.
"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte," the statement said.
Drawing from his real-life experience with cerebral palsy, Mitte was best known for his breakout role on the AMC cable TV series Breaking Bad, playing the only son of the lead character, Walter White, a terminally ill high school teacher who descends into a secret life of crime cooking crystal meth.
Mitte's character, who adopted the nickname Flynn, used crutches and spoke with a slur, gains greater prominence as the story arc of the series progressed. He starts out as a carefree teenager who largely admires his father but later struggles to reckon with the family' disintegration as the truth about Walter White's "Heisenberg" alter ego emerges.
"Mitte brought authenticity to the role and built a platform on disability awareness and inclusion," the statement said, noting that the actor was active in a number of philanthropic organizations devoted to fundraising and awareness for cerebral palsy and other muscle-control disorders.
The acclaimed series, often cited by critics as one of the best television dramas of all time, ran from 2008-2013, garnering 16 Emmy awards, including two for best drama series.
He later played a high school wrestler with cerebral palsy in the 2021 coming-of-age drama Triumph. He was a Screen Actors Guild spokesman for performers with disabilities, and a celebrity ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy.

Source: Reuters/mm

items.summary: India has outlined plans to become a major green hydrogen producer, even as developers worldwide have struggled to secure the long-term offtake agreements required to underpin large-scale investments ...
items.body:
Home / Companies / News / NTPC in talks with Japan, South Korea, Germany for sale of green fuel

NTPC in talks with Japan, South Korea, Germany for sale of green fuel India has outlined plans to become a major green hydrogen producer, even as developers worldwide have struggled to secure the long-term offtake agreements required to underpin large-scale investments

NTPC is in talks with prospective overseas customers as it develops a proposed green hydrogen hub in Andhra Pradesh | Image: Bloomberg

Reuters NEW DELHI 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 12:39 PM IST

Listen to This Article

India's top power producer NTPC is in talks with potential buyers in Japan, South Korea and Germany for green ammonia and other low-carbon fuels, Chairman Gurdeep Singh said on Tuesday.
India has outlined plans to become a major green hydrogen producer, even as developers worldwide have struggled to secure the long-term offtake agreements required to underpin large-scale investments.
NTPC is in talks with prospective overseas customers as it develops a proposed green hydrogen hub in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh, Singh said at an event organised by the Indian Chamber of Commerce.
The project is expected to produce green ammonia and green methanol, which are considered more practical than hydrogen for transportation and international trade.
 

"We have to make hydrogen a business," Singh said, adding that the focus was shifting from pilot projects to commercially viable ventures.

Backed by subsidies of roughly $2.1 billion, New Delhi aims to produce 5 million metric tons of green hydrogen annually by 2030.
Demand for green fuels is expected to rise as industries look for alternatives to fossil fuels to reduce missions and meet decarbonisation targets.

items.title: Japan's wholesale inflation remains elevated, keeps alive BOJ rate-hike view
items.author: Leika Kihara
items.creator: Leika Kihara
items.summary: The data highlights mounting inflationary pressure that keeps alive market expectations of a near-term interest rate hike.
items.body:
Japan's wholesale prices rose 6.8% in the year to September, according to data released on Tuesday, slowing from the previous month but highlighting mounting inflationary pressure that keeps alive market expectations of a near-term interest rate hike.
The data will be among the factors that the Bank of Japan will scrutinise when its board produces fresh quarterly growth and inflation forecasts at this month's policy meeting.
The rise in the corporate goods price index, which measures the price companies charge each other for their goods and services, compared with the median market forecast for a 7.6% increase. It slowed from a 7.6% gain in August.
The yen-based import price index surged 24.5% in September from a year earlier, the data released by the BOJ showed, a sign that the currency's weakness continued to push up the cost of raw material imports.
"Wholesale inflation will likely re-accelerate given strong uncertainty over the Middle East conflict, which is keeping crude oil prices elevated," said Masato Koike, a senior economist at Sompo Institute Plus.
"But there's no sign of inflationary pressure accelerating sharply for the time being," heightening the chance that the BOJ will stand pat in October and wait until December to raise interest rates again, he said.
Speaking in parliament on Tuesday, BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda [USN:SPN45900V TEXT:"said"] underlying inflation "has now come quite close to 2%."
Unlike in the past, when the aim of monetary policy was to lift underlying inflation toward 2%, Ueda said the economy "has entered a phase where an important policy objective is to keep it stable at around that level."
On Tuesday, a separate BOJ survey [USN:P8N45R035 TEXT:"showed"] that the ratio of Japanese households expecting prices to rise five years from now increased to 86.5% from 86.1% in the previous survey in June, suggesting inflation expectations remain firmly entrenched.
At the same time, the pace of expected inflation moderated, with households projecting prices to rise by an average of 11.8% in a year's time, down from 13.1%, and by 10.1% annually over the next five years, compared with 10.8% in the previous survey.
BOJ EYES PASS-THROUGH A recent spike in wholesale inflation was among the factors that the BOJ cited as evidence of mounting price pressures behind its decision to raise interest rates in June and September.
While the prices of farm products fell 13.3% in September from a year earlier due largely to plunging prices for rice, a broad range of other goods recorded price rises, including processed food, electric machinery and telecommunications equipment, the data showed.
Prices of chemical goods rose 13.3%, plastic products increased 12.8% and non-ferrous metals goods were up 40.2%, a sign of the increasing cost firms were facing from the weak yen, the US-Israeli war on Iran and robust AI-related demand, the data showed.
Governor Ueda has said the key to the pace and timing of future rate hikes would be the extent to which such upward pressure on wholesale prices spreads to consumer inflation, as well as how that could affect consumption.
Recent data showed [USN:L4N45M0C3 TEXT:"core consumer inflation in Tokyo"], which is considered a leading indicator of nationwide price trends, accelerated in September at its fastest pace in 10 months.
[USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"Sources have told Reuters"] the BOJ may signal this month that underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2% target, highlighting its readiness to raise rates again in the coming months.
The BOJ raised its key rate to a 31-year high [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"last month"], while signalling its entry into a phase focused on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its target, raising the prospect of tighter policy.
At the meeting on October 29 and 30, the BOJ will release fresh quarterly growth and inflation forecasts that will be closely watched by market participants for clues to the timing of the next rate hike. [USN:L4N44Z0P0 TEXT:"Many analysts"] expect the central bank to raise interest rates again by the end of this year.

NYT, Economist among publishers joining coalition to curb unpaid AI use

FAST

Oct 12 : The New York Times, Agence France-Presse and The Economist on Monday joined more than 40 publishers in a coalition aimed at preventing AI firms from using or profiting from their content without permission.
The Standards for Publisher Usage Rights (SPUR) coalition, launched in February, now has more than 80 members across over 20 countries. New members include The Atlantic and Brazil's National Association of Newspapers, joining founding members such as the Financial Times, BBC and Associated Press.
Publishers are stepping up legal efforts to prevent AI companies from using their content without permission to train large language models. Earlier this month, USA Today and several newspapers it owns sued OpenAI, alleging copyright infringement.
OpenAI and its backer, Microsoft, also face similar copyright claims from prominent authors and news organizations, including the New York Times.

SPUR, which is funded entirely by its members, is developing industry-wide standards and technical systems to help publishers track and control how AI companies use their content and facilitate licensing agreements, according to its website.
"Intellectual property protection and technological advancement can and must co-exist," Rebecca Grossman-Cohen, the New York Times' head of strategic partnerships and chief of staff, said in a statement.
Publishers are also grappling with declining referral traffic as search engines roll out AI-generated answers that allow users to consume information without clicking through to websites.
Google organic-search referrals to more than 2,500 websites fell 33 per cent globally between November 2024 and November 2025, according to a Reuters Institute report, citing data from Chartbeat.
SPUR said it recently introduced its Content Telemetry Standard, designed to standardize how AI agents record and report their use of media content, as part of efforts to ensure creators are compensated for their work.

Source: Reuters

items.title: India 'mother of democracy', does not grow at anyone's expense: PM Modi
items.summary: Citing India's linguistic diversity and digital reach, PM Modi said that technology, data and knowledge are redefining power, which should be used to empower people and create new opportunities ...
items.body:
Home / India News / India 'mother of democracy', does not grow at anyone's expense: PM Modi

India 'mother of democracy', does not grow at anyone's expense: PM Modi Citing India's linguistic diversity and digital reach, PM Modi said that technology, data and knowledge are redefining power, which should be used to empower people and create new opportunities

Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, in New Delhi | Image: PTI

Apexa Rai New Delhi 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 11:30 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said India does not believe in growing in isolation or withholding knowledge, but favours sharing its capabilities and working with other countries.
  Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum , PM Modi said, “India does not grow at anyone's expense. We grow with the world and for the world."
  Calling India the “mother of democracy”, PM Modi said the country’s linguistic diversity and wide-ranging media landscape reflected the many ways people access information and discuss issues.
  He said India had more than 100 languages, around 80,000 registered newspapers and publications, and over 1,000 satellite television channels.
  India's digital reach has further expanded the avenues for public discussion, he said, pointing to more than 500 million YouTube users and over 500 million Instagram users.

  “In our country, people openly debate different issues and discuss different perspectives,” PM Modi said, adding that digital power had played a significant role in enabling such exchanges.
  He said power in the 21st century should be measured by how it is used and whether it benefits a wider section of society.
  “The question is not who has power, but how that power is being used,” he said, highlighting the need to use knowledge to create opportunities rather than concentrate it in the hands of a few.   ALSO READ: PM Modi unveils ₹13K cr projects in TN, vows to work for state's growth

Affordable data has expanded access PM Modi also pointed to developments in India's digital ecosystem since 2014, saying affordable mobile data had helped extend access to digital services and learning opportunities.
  He cited remote digital learning, online classes and the ability of shopkeepers in remote areas to use digital tools as examples of how connectivity could expand opportunities beyond major urban centres.

items.title: "We grow with the world and for the world": PM Modi highlights startup growth, digital innovation
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday highlighted India's digital ecosystem and the role of technology in promoting inclusion, citing the country's digital payment platform as an example of how ...
items.body:
"We grow with the world and for the world": PM Modi highlights startup growth, digital innovation Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday highlighted India's digital ecosystem and the role of technology in promoting inclusion, citing the country's digital payment platform as an example of how businesses of different scales can access the same system.
ANI | Updated: 13-10-2026 11:13 IST | Created: 13-10-2026 11:13 IST

Prime Minister Narendra Modi (Photo/DD). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

India

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday highlighted India's digital ecosystem and the role of technology in promoting inclusion, citing the country's digital payment platform as an example of how businesses of different scales can access the same system. "We do not grow at anyone's cost. We grow with the world and for the world," the PM said while addressing a gathering at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum.
PM Modi described India as the “Mother of Democracy” while highlighting its linguistic diversity, media landscape and growing social media user base as examples of the country's openness to different perspectives. “India is the Mother of Democracy. India has over 100 languages, around 80,000 registered newspapers and publications, and more than 1,000 satellite television channels,” the Prime Minister said.
Highlighting India's digital reach, PM Modi said the country had more than 500 million YouTube users and over 500 million Instagram users. He added that people in India openly debated issues and discussed different perspectives, with digital power playing a significant role in facilitating these exchanges. Inviting international delegates to experience India's digital payment ecosystem, the Prime Minister encouraged them to try the country's digital payment facilities.
“I would tell the guests who have come from abroad to try India's digital payment ecosystem,” PM Modi said. Explaining how the system accommodates businesses of different sizes, Pm Modi said a street vendor and a car showroom operator, despite differences in their businesses and scale of operations, could use the same digital payment platform in India.
“In our country, a street vendor and a car showroom have different kinds of businesses and operate at different scales, but in India, both use the same digital payment platform,” he said. Emphasising the importance of making technology accessible across economic segments, the Prime Minister said, “This is the power of inclusive technology.”
PM Modi remarks highlighted India's approach to using digital infrastructure to expand access to technology and payment services for businesses of varying sizes. Prime Minister also highlighted India's growth in startups and digital innovation, stating that the number of startups in the country has increased from a few hundred before 2014 to over 2.5 lakh.
PM Modi said opportunities for innovation were reaching more people, with nearly half of startups coming from small cities and towns and 45 per cent having a woman director or partner. “Before 2014, there were only a few hundred startups in India; now, their number in the country has exceeded 2.5 lakh,” the Prime Minister said.
Highlighting the growing participation of people from different regions and backgrounds in the startup ecosystem, PM Modi said, “Nearly half of the startups come from small cities and towns. 45% of startups have a woman director or partner.” “In other words, opportunities for innovation are reaching more people, and more talents are emerging,” he added.
The Prime Minister said India was also sharing its experience with Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) with other countries to help them develop digital systems suited to their needs. “We are sharing our experience with Digital Public Infrastructure with other countries so that they can develop their digital systems according to their needs,” PM Modi said.
Referring to India's digital initiatives during the COVID-19 pandemic, PM Modi said the country had developed the CoWIN platform as an open-source system. He said India's capabilities should help create opportunities for other countries as well. “During COVID-19, we also created the CoWIN platform, which was open source. Our continuous efforts are aimed at ensuring that India’s capabilities open new doors of possibility for other countries as well. In other words, our capabilities should empower humanity,” he said.
Emphasising the wider significance of innovation, PM Modi said turning ideas into products and problems into solutions was an important capability, but its impact increased when more people had access to such opportunities. “Friends, the power of innovation is also like this. Turning an idea into a product and a problem into a solution is a great capability in itself. But when more and more people in society get this opportunity, the balance of power is maintained, and its impact increases manifold,” the Prime Minister said.
PM Modi also highlighted the role of technology in improving the delivery of government assistance, saying it had enabled direct transfers to beneficiaries' bank accounts. “Using technology, we have created a system to transfer government assistance directly to the bank accounts of beneficiaries,” he said.
The Prime Minister added that the system had helped reduce corruption, improved convenience for citizens, and established a direct channel between the government and the people. The eighth edition of the Bloomberg New Economy Forum (the “Forum”), hosted in India, convenes more than 500 of the world’s most influential public and private sector leaders.
Under the theme “A World in Play: Defining the New Levers of Power”, delegates will examine the changing state of geopolitics, identify the risks and opportunities presented by this period of uncertainty, exchange ideas, and collaborate on a roadmap toward future prosperity. (ANI)
